Jonas — thanks for the context and for attaching the redline. I reviewed the doc and grouped comments:

1) Commercial terms: payment net-45 in our redline is fine; Everwell requested net-60 in their mark but offered to accommodate for the pilot. This is negotiable at the order form level — not a blocker for registration.

2) Liability / indemnity: Everwell struck a clause that would add insurer subrogation carveouts. That needs a short conversation; we can suggest the standard Redwood carveout language but it is not a deal-breaker for a pilot order form.

3) Data security / SOC: their mark adds a narrow exception for production telemetry. We need their SOC2 report + POA&M for any exceptions.

Recommendation: allow order form signature for pilot if the following are provided and validated before Coupa activation: COI naming Redwood as additional insured (see attachment sample), the W-9 (provided), and SOC2 report link or attestation (partial evidence acceptable for pilot with a remediation plan).

I uploaded a redlined MSA with inline guidance: https://docs.redwood.com/shared/everwell-msaredline-v3 (internal). If Legal wants to keep working the MSA in parallel we can, but for speed I recommend procurement grant temporary activation for pilot with a strict evidence handback and a 30-day MSA finalization checkpoint.

Action items (Legal / Procurement / Ops):
- Kimberly: confirm whether ProcureTech can set supplier status to "Pending-Active" (or equivalent) conditioned on COI/W-9/SOC2 upload.
- Jonas: confirm with Everwell that they'll accept a pilot order form signature and commit to the 30-day MSA wrap-up.
- Markus: confirm acceptable COI wording and whether an endorsement is required now or can be uploaded within 14 days.

Thanks — procurement checked with ProcureTech. Summary of portal gating and next steps: 

Portal gating checklist (ProcureTech):
- Tax ID (W-9) match: pass (Everwell_W9.pdf)
- COI: must show coverage lines (Cyber/Errors & Omissions preferred) and list Redwood Inference as additional insured or have an endorsement uploaded within 14 days of activation.
- Bank verification: required for ACH setup (bank_verification_Everwell.pdf attached).
- Authorized signer: ProcureTech requires the uploaded order form to show the signatory name and title that matches entity records or notarized delegation for signature by someone else.

ProcureTech has a "Pre-Active (Pilot)" status they can assign if Legal confirms the pilot order form is acceptable and a firm remediation milestone is defined. They will accept COI as a soft-check if an endorsement is promised within 14 days, but under special cases they require endorsement before first invoice.

Procurement asks for one consolidated zip of evidence (W-9, COI, bank letter, signed order form) uploaded to the ProcureTech portal. They prefer a DocuSign envelope link for the signed order form (we can send the DocuSign once Legal signs off).

I attached a sample COI template for reference (Everwell_COI.pdf). I will open the request with ProcureTech and hold for Legal confirmation on the pilot approach.

Next steps / owners:
- Marissa: confirm pilot-approved order form language (short note in the redline will suffice).
- Jonas: tell Everwell we can accept pilot order form and request DocuSign envelope to avoid manual upload errors.
- Markus: confirm COI endorsement deadline you can accept (14 days?)
